analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leverkusen host the bottom side the week after their trip to Dortmund, and both teams' league games have averaged more than four goals. The brief lists Ko Itakura as missing, but his one-match ban will have been served against Dortmund, and Gladbach hope to have Tim Kleindienst back, though they took one win from their first nine games under two coaches.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. I lean higher: Leverkusen's games and Gladbach's have both produced 37 goals in nine, with Gladbach conceding 25. Carles Martínez's side scored at least twice in each of its first ten competitive games.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners. Leverkusen's possession game against a Gladbach side likely to sit deep in a back three or five should produce plenty of corners for the hosts, so I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already high. Leverkusen's games have been card-heavy and Gladbach's frustration has shown, but the number already reflects both, so I stay level.

shots.text: The site has 31.6 shots. That is a lot, but Leverkusen at home against a defence that concedes nearly three a game should get there, and Gladbach's share depends on whether Kleindienst is back. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Gladbach's defence lets opponents hit the target often, and Leverkusen have Patrik Schick, who scored in the derby, in form.
